wire.t: Kenneth Walker III is still starting for I Pulled My McCaff on Sunday morning, and Hing1eMcCring13berry hasn't made a waiver move this week. The Chiefs ruled Walker out Friday with a groin injury, and the only bench backs, Blake Corum and Dylan Sampson, are on bye.

stories.title: Six hours to kickoff, Kenneth Walker III is still in the I Pulled My McCaff lineup, and the waiver wire is still sitting there
stories.dek: No add, no drop, no running back. Plus the Brock Bowers call, the Mike Evans swap that's sitting on a bench, and the one Arizona quarterback change that just paid Slippery Balls.
body: As of 7 a.m. Sunday, Hing1eMcCring13berry has made zero waiver moves this week, and Kenneth Walker III is still starting at running back for I Pulled My McCaff. The Chiefs ruled him out Friday. Blake Corum and Dylan Sampson are on bye, so there's no swap on the roster. There is a waiver wire, and it has running backs on it, and any one of them is worth more than 0.0. I Pulled My McCaff leads Rome Alone 15.80 to 1.80 and is a 15.1-point favorite, so it can probably survive a zero. Probably. Free agency locks at kickoff, Hing1eMcCring13berry. Click something.

The Brock Bowers call is a true game-time decision. He's questionable at Denver with ankle and quad injuries, and Klint Kubiak didn't commit either way Friday. tballsmccall has Sam LaPorta on the bench as the backup, which is the right setup, and the Raiders-Broncos kickoff is late enough to see the inactives first. If Bowers sits, Michael Mayer takes the Raiders tight end snaps, and Marco_Polo has Mayer on the Rome Alone bench. Nobody in this league has ever been that prepared on purpose.

DuvalTiliFall has the cleanest fix on the board: Mike Evans is questionable with Achilles tendinitis, Keenan Allen plays for the same 49ers team, and Allen is on the Likely Cookin That Diaper bench. Check the inactives, swap if needed, done. And Shootyeah got lucky without lifting a finger: Carson Beck didn't practice Friday, Josh Johnson is expected to start for Arizona, and Slippery Balls starts the Chiefs defense in a game Kansas City is favored to win by 15.5.

Elsewhere: Ladd McConkey is questionable for MarcusbetterLockNjigba with no real backup, Baker Mayfield is questionable in Detroit, and Kirk Cousins starts for Minnesota with Kyler Murray out, which is now Justin Jefferson's problem and therefore my problem. My lineup is set, C.J. Stroud's 21.46 is banked, and I'm up 18.16. If I lose this from here, I'll shotgun two.

columns.title: The Matchup of the Week is the only game left that decides anything
columns.dek: Rome Alone is at 63 percent and down 15.80 to 1.80. I Pulled My McCaff has a zero at running back. Somebody is about to find out what they are.
body: Every week this site picks a Matchup of the Week, and most weeks it's a nice idea. This week it's the whole season for one team. Rome Alone is 6‑4, sixth in the standings and at 63 percent in Erection Projections. Your Mom’s Magic Dick is at 42 percent and coming hard. Lose this one and Marco_Polo is staring at a coin flip for the last spot.

The opponent is I Pulled My McCaff, the best team in the league by points, 1,418.22 of them, and an 86‑24 all-play. It's up 15.80 to 1.80 after Thursday. And it's starting a running back who has been ruled out, because the two guys behind him are on bye. That's not a mistake. That's a hole, and Hing1eMcCring13berry has until Sunday at 1 to fill it.

I'm hearing CeeDee Lamb has asked Marco_Polo to set the Rome Alone lineup before Wednesday from now on. Word is he heard about the four empty slots on Wednesday and asked for a locker room where the lineup exists before he does.

So here's where it stands. Rome Alone needs CeeDee Lamb, Caleb Williams and Ashton Jeanty to outscore Christian McCaffrey, Jayden Daniels and Malik Nabers by more than 14 with a possible zero on the other side helping. It can happen! But this is the team that started two inactive receivers a week ago, and I've seen how this movie ends. MARCO_POLO, SET THE LINEUP AND PRAY.

columns.title: Sunday morning tape: every lineup with a problem, graded before kickoff
columns.dek: One lineup has a known zero in it. Two have a game-time call with the answer on the bench. One got bailed out by an Arizona depth chart.
body: Film session. Lineups as of 7 a.m. Sunday. I grade what's on the screen, not what you meant to do.

I Pulled My McCaff. Kenneth Walker III ruled out Friday. Still starting. Blake Corum on bye. Dylan Sampson on bye. Not a dumb roster call, there's nobody to slide in. But the wire's open and there's been zero moves all week. Up 14.00 with a zero in the backfield. Grade: Incomplete. Turns into a C if a waiver back is in by 1.

MarcusbetterLockNjigba. Brock Bowers questionable, game-time decision. Sam LaPorta on the bench. That's how you build it. Ladd McConkey questionable with no real backup behind him. Down 18.16 and Seattle's on bye. Grade: B for the setup, and it drops to a D if Bowers sits and nobody's watching.

Likely Cookin That Diaper. Mike Evans questionable. Keenan Allen, same team, same kickoff, on the bench. That's a free swap. Grade: B+ now. A if DuvalTiliFall checks the inactives, F if he doesn't. Last week he sat Tony Pollard's 23.9 and lost by 15.94. I'm not giving him the benefit of the doubt.

Word around the Likely Cookin That Diaper locker room is that Keenan Allen has started sitting at the end of the bench with his helmet already on, just in case. Sources say he's told teammates he likes DuvalTiliFall fine but would like to be told things before kickoff, not after.

Slippery Balls. Did nothing. Kansas City defense got Josh Johnson anyway. Grade: A for luck, D for effort. McCallyCockin(his butt). C.J. Stroud's 21.46 banked, lineup full, up 18.16. Grade: B. I'm not giving the guy who signs my checks an A. That's integrity.

columns.title: Five Sunday-morning moves every contender should make before 1 p.m.
columns.dek: Your Senior Fantasy Strategist (self-appointed) has studied the inactives, the waiver wire and his own heart. Here's the plan.
body: I've been up since 4. The coffee is strong and so are my convictions. Five moves, in order of importance.

1. Hing1eMcCring13berry: don't add a running back. I Pulled My McCaff leads by 14.00 and scores 141.8 a week. Adding a waiver back would be admitting there's a problem, and confidence is a stat. A running back slot with nobody playing in it is the purest form of trust.

2. tballsmccall: start Brock Bowers and Sam LaPorta together. Two tight ends is double the tight end. You'll have to bench Ladd McConkey, but McConkey is questionable and LaPorta has no designation, and a healthy tight end is just a receiver who's been to the gym.

3. DuvalTiliFall: leave Mike Evans in no matter what. Swapping in Keenan Allen sends a message to the locker room that being healthy matters, and that's a slippery slope. Likely Cookin That Diaper is 7‑3. Don't fix what got you to 7‑3.

Sources say Isaiah Likely has asked DuvalTiliFall to rename the team after somebody else. I'm told he loves the 28.7 he scored for Likely Cookin That Diaper but feels the name has put a lot of diaper-related pressure on him, and he'd like a more mature locker-room vibe heading into December.

4. Marco_Polo: start Michael Mayer over Colston Loveland, just in case Brock Bowers sits. And 5. Shootyeah: bench the Kansas City defense. Everybody knows Josh Johnson is starting. When everybody knows something, it's already priced in. That's just strategy.

columns.title: The Week 11 defense payout, modeled: I have Slippery Balls winning money
columns.dek: Houston has 15.0 banked. Kansas City is a 15.5-point favorite against a questionable quarterback. The math has spoken.
body: Here are the inputs. The Week 11 payout goes to the highest-scoring starting defense. The Houston defense has 15.0 for Your Mom’s Magic Dick. The best defense in Week 10 was the Vikings at 21.0. Eleven starting defenses are still to play, and one of them, Kansas City, is a 15.5-point home favorite over Arizona, whose quarterback Carson Beck is questionable with a back injury.

Here is the model. Slippery Balls starts the Kansas City defense. Slippery Balls is 3‑7 and at 0 percent to make the playoffs. Teams with nothing left to play for have nothing left to lose, and a defense with nothing to lose takes the ball away. Therefore Shootyeah wins the Week 11 payout. I'd put the confidence at 100 percent, but I round up.

Sources say Saquon Barkley wants a better locker-room vibe at Slippery Balls and has asked Shootyeah to stop referring to the playoffs as 'a social construct.' I'm told Barkley has been seen browsing the Allen-tents & Purposes roster page for an open running back spot, and there isn't one.

One more number for the skeptics. Slippery Balls has scored 1,010.26 points this season, 11th in the league, and its weekly standard deviation is 18.7, the third smallest. That means it is reliably bad, and reliability is the most important trait in a defense. I don't take questions about this.

items.label: Matchup of the Week
items.title: I Pulled My McCaff vs. Rome Alone: the biggest total on the board, and the last playoff spot on the line
items.dek: A 260.6 total, the most points in the league against the team holding the sixth seed, and Marco_Polo still has a can to drink.
body: This is the game with the most points in it. I Pulled My McCaff scores 141.8 a week, the best in the league, with an 86‑24 all-play. Rome Alone scores 118.8 a week. Put them together and the total is 260.6, highest of Week 11 by 10.9.

And it's the one with the stakes. Rome Alone is 6‑4, sixth in the standings and at 62 percent in Erection Projections, the last team inside the line. Your Mom’s Magic Dick is right behind at 43 percent. I Pulled My McCaff is at 96 percent to make it and 46 percent for a bye, so Hing1eMcCring13berry is playing for the top two.

The byes cut both ways. I Pulled My McCaff loses Blake Corum, KC Concepcion Jr. and Dylan Sampson to byes, and Kenneth Walker III is out, so Christian McCaffrey carries the backfield. Rome Alone gets Caleb Williams, Bucky Irving, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland back but loses the Rams defense. That cuts a 23.1-point gap to 15.1.
The pick: I Pulled My McCaff by 15.1, 69 percent. Marco_Polo has the bodies back. Now he has to put them in the lineup.
items.result: After Thursday: I Pulled My McCaff 15.80, Rome Alone 1.80. Kenneth Walker III (out) is still in the I Pulled My McCaff lineup Sunday morning.

items.label: Shit Show of the Week
items.title: Your Mom’s Magic Dick vs. Skatabooboo: the lowest total of the week, and an 0‑10 team
items.dek: 205.2 projected points combined, 55 below the Matchup of the Week. Skatabooboo has been eliminated for weeks.
body: The sewer game this week is Your Mom’s Magic Dick against Skatabooboo, with a projected total of 205.2, the lowest on the board by 19.0. Skatabooboo scores 85.2 a week, the worst in the league by 15.8, and is 0‑10.

Playoff implications: one side only. Skatabooboo is out. Your Mom’s Magic Dick is 5‑5 at 43 percent, so the only thing that matters here is Cavemanfsu not becoming the answer to a trivia question by losing to the winless team.

Your Mom’s Magic Dick is hot, three straight wins at 149.46 a week, and only loses bench guys (Matthew Stafford, Konata Mumpfield, Denzel Boston) to byes. Skatabooboo gets Courtland Sutton back from his bye but loses Tutu Atwell. Cam Skattebo scored 27.2 last week and is the only reason to watch.
The pick: Your Mom’s Magic Dick by 33.8, 86 percent. ClaytonBigsbi, there's always Week 12.
items.result: After Thursday: Skatabooboo 18.60, Your Mom’s Magic Dick 15.00. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Trey McBride play Sunday.

items.title: Allen-tents & Purposes over JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson by 34.1: the biggest spread of Week 11
items.dek: The first-place team, three straight wins and its backups back from byes, against a team at 3 percent.
body: Allen-tents & Purposes scores 140.1 a week with a 79‑31 all-play. JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson scores 108.0. That's a 32.1-point gap before anyone checks the injury report.

Then you check it. JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson loses Zach Charbonnet to the Seattle bye, and Jaylen Waddle and Jake Ferguson are out. Allen-tents & Purposes loses Matthew Golden and the Seahawks defense but gets Dallas Goedert, Jonah Coleman and D’Andre Swift back from Week 10 byes. That's 34.1.

Stakes: Allen-tents & Purposes is at 84 percent for a bye and wants the top seed. JTWaddlesHisPurdyJohnson is 5‑5 and at 3 percent; it needs to win out and get help. Brock Purdy scored 33.66 last week, and GeorigaGoocher needs another one of those plus a Jahmyr Gibbs dud.
The pick: Allen-tents & Purposes by 34.1, 86 percent. RedDevil904 should be done by Sunday afternoon.
